overall: Violation found: the June 29 notice omitted the Town Counsel candidate for reappointment. The Board was ordered to comply immediately and in future. A footnote flags an unnoticed 'Special Counsel' discussion, but makes no formal finding on it.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the June 29 meeting notice lacked sufficient specificity because it did not name the candidate for Town Counsel reappointment.
allegations.key_passage: The Board acknowledges, and we find, that it violated the Open Meeting Law because the meeting notice did not identify the candidate for Town Counsel.

allegations.summary: Not alleged in the complaint; a footnote says discussion of an individual 'Special Counsel' attorney outside the main counsel firm should have been in the notice.
allegations.key_passage: This topic and the identity of this individual attorney should have been included in the meeting notice.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and caution that future similar violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
